newsitem.title: USA: Armey repeats sees budget resolution vote in May.
newsitem.headline: Armey repeats sees budget resolution vote in May.

text.p: House Majority Leader Dick Armey repeated Tuesday that he expected a budget resolution to go to the House floor for a vote in May.
The budget resolution is essentially a budget blueprint, and the deadline of April 15 is not expected to be met.

The House Tuesday will consider a resolution calling on President Clinton to resubmit his budget, Armey said. Republicans have criticized Clinton's budget, saying it does not reach balance in 2002 and ultimately results in tax increases. The White House says Clinton's budget does reach balance.
"I am still optimistic and have every expectation that we will have a budget proposal on the floor of the House in the first couple of weeks of May at the latest," Armey said.
"What we're trying to avoid, and what is not productive, is to sort of have a standoff between our budget and your budget," the Texas Republican said.
"We don't look for a wrangle over this; we look for an opportunity for them (White House) to reassess it and give us their best recommendations how to fix it," he said.
